status.label: Confirm the reported modifier-sticking case
status.detail: The report says remapping Alt+Shift+Esc to Ctrl+Shift+Esc opens Task Manager but can leave Ctrl or Shift stuck; the broader tracker #31571 covers related modifier-state failures.

judgment.rationale: The report gives a concrete shortcut substitution and says the action succeeds while Ctrl or Shift remains logically pressed. Open tracker #31571 covers related sticky-modifier symptoms, but this exact successful-chord/stuck-key case is not shown to be the same mechanism. Current-build reproduction and the specific mapping state are needed before deciding whether it belongs under that tracker or needs a distinct fix.
evidence: The report lists PowerToys 0.81.1 and says remapping Alt+Shift+Esc to Ctrl+Shift+Esc opens Task Manager but can leave Ctrl or Shift stuck.
The reporter says running PowerToys in administrator mode resolved the symptom for them.
The issue's similarity bot links open tracker #31571, a broad Keyboard Manager modifier-sticking thread.
The only comment is an automated similar-issues notice; no maintainer reproduction is documented.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce the reported modifier remap on current stable in normal and administrator modes, then compare the exact stuck-state result with the open #31571 tracker.

fix_assessment.rationale: If the remapped chord leaves an unmatched Ctrl or Shift key state, Keyboard Manager should balance the injected modifier lifecycle. The report's administrator-mode workaround and related tracker are useful comparison points, but the current mechanism is not established.

proposed_fixes.title: Balance modifier state for remapped multi-key shortcuts
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The remap may emit Ctrl+Shift+Esc successfully but fail to balance one injected modifier's key-up state under the reported execution context; this needs reproduction.
plan: Reproduce the Alt+Shift+Esc-to-Ctrl+Shift+Esc mapping on current stable and record which modifier, if any, remains active.

verification: The remapped shortcut opens Task Manager and leaves Ctrl, Shift, and Alt released.

reproduce.title: Check modifier release after remapped Task Manager shortcut
prerequisites: Ability to test supported normal and administrator execution modes
steps: Trigger the remapped shortcut in normal execution mode and verify Task Manager opens.
Use unrelated keyboard input to check whether Ctrl, Shift, or Alt remains active.
Repeat in administrator execution mode and compare the result.
If a modifier sticks, identify which one and whether releasing the source keys changes its state.
reproduce.expected_result: The remapped shortcut opens Task Manager and all source and destination modifiers return to released state.
